identity.real_world_identity_notes: Brazilian sports prototype built by Metalmoro, raced in Imperio Endurance Brasil. The chassis is shared across the class's engine options; the name denotes the engine rather than the marque. A Judd-engined AJR is not documented by the registered source, which lists only Chevrolet LS3 and Honda K20 engines. This configuration is treated as simulator content rather than a documented real car.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: automatic cut on upshifts and automatic blip on downshifts, so the driver supplies neither.
The clutch is not needed to pull away.
No reviewed source documents a Judd-engined AJR. The gearbox and chassis come from the documented AJR; the engine is recorded as an unverified simulator configuration.
Community references for this car are generated from Coanda's AMS2 spreadsheet, so they describe the simulator rather than the real car and are not cited here as real-world evidence.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.metalmoro-ajr-judd.20260816t151456905z-e3febd0b by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.

claims.basis: The registered source establishes the AJR chassis and gearbox. It does not document a Judd-engined car, so only the chassis identity is carried and the engine is not claimed.
The registered source gives the AJR a six-speed sequential semi-automatic gearbox, and the live drive selected six paddle gears with automatic cut and blip.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.
